data.question_title: \(\text{A\({}_{1}\)}\) g of an element give \(\text{A\({}_{2}\)}\) g of its oxide. The equivalent mass of the element is:
data.explanation_txt:
Mass of oxygen in the oxide = \(A_2-A_1\)

\(A_2-A_1\) gram of oxygen combines with \(A_1\) gram of element

1 gram of oxygen combines with \(\cfrac{A_1}{A_2-A_1}\) gram of the element.

Equivalent mass of oxygen = 8

\(\therefore\) 8 gram of oxygen combines with \(\cfrac{A_1}{A_2-A_1}\times 8\) gram of the element.

And as always 1 equivalent weight of an element combines with 1 equivalent weight of that compound.

Hence, equivalent weight of the element = \(\cfrac{A_1}{A_2-A_1}\times 8\)

data.explanation_txt:
No. of gram equivalents of HCl left after the reaction between metal carbonate and HCl = 0.005*1 = 0.005 gram equivalents

No. of gram equivalents present in metal carbonate = 0.025*1 - 0.005 = 0.02 gram equivalents

Equivalent weight of metal carbonate = \(\cfrac{\text{Amount in gm}}{\text{No. of gram equivalents}}\) = \(\cfrac{1}{0.02}\) = 50
